$comment: Lakebase fit-checker. Each option carries a flag (green/yellow/red). Verdict rules live in 'verdicts'. Edit freely; validated at startup.
title: Is Lakebase a good fit?
intro: Answer a few questions about the workload you are considering. The checker flags blockers and risks early, so you qualify opportunities honestly.

options.label: Transactional app, agent state, or low-latency feature/data serving
Transactional plus a meaningful amount of analytical querying on the same database
options.note: Keep heavy analytics in the lakehouse; use synced tables or Lakehouse Sync instead of scanning the operational database.

options.label: Large-scale reporting or OLAP directly on the operational database
options.note: Lakebase is an OLTP database. Run analytical workloads on the lakehouse instead of splitting data across branches or projects to work around limits.

questions.prompt: Where does the data live today?

options.label: Already on PostgreSQL (or new, nothing to migrate)
Another relational database that must be migrated
options.note: Assess migration readiness first and plan a phased migration; expect schema and SQL dialect work.

options.label: A NoSQL or GraphQL-centric system
options.note: Moving from non-Postgres, non-relational models is a re-architecture, not a lift-and-shift.

questions.prompt: How many concurrent connections at peak?

options.label: Roughly 1,000 to 4,000
options.note: Use application-side pooling and size the compute to the connection budget for your maximum CU.

options.label: More than 4,000
options.note: Connections are capped at 4,000 per endpoint; redesign with pooling or fewer clients.

options.label: 2 TB to 8 TB
options.note: Within limits, but plan capacity, backups and restore windows carefully.

options.label: More than 8 TB
options.note: Exceeds the per-branch logical data limit; consider archiving cold data or partitioning by workload.

questions.prompt: How much low-level Postgres tuning does the workload need?

options.label: Some tuning of queries and indexes (application level)
Depends on tuning server parameters such as autovacuum, work_mem or shared_buffers
options.note: Those server parameters are not configurable on Lakebase; validate with a proof of concept before committing.

options.label: Only common supported ones (for example pgvector, pg_stat_statements, pgcrypto, PostGIS)
Not sure yet
options.note: List what the app uses and compare it with SELECT * FROM pg_available_extensions.

options.label: Extensions that manipulate Postgres storage directly
options.note: Extensions that change the storage layer are not supported.

questions.prompt: How does the data relate to the lakehouse?

options.label: Serve lakehouse data to an app, or analyse operational data in the lakehouse
No lakehouse interaction planned
options.note: Lakebase still works as managed Postgres, but the integration advantage is smaller; confirm the value case.

questions.prompt: Is Lakebase available in the required cloud region?

options.label: Not checked yet
options.note: Check the current regional availability list before positioning a date.

options.label: No
options.note: Data residency may rule it out until the region is supported.

good.label: Good fit
good.summary: No blockers found. Proceed to a proof of concept and confirm the details below.

caution.label: Proceed with care
caution.summary: No hard blockers, but several risks need answers before you commit.

notYet.label: Not a fit today
notYet.summary: At least one blocker makes Lakebase a poor match as described. Resolve or redesign before proceeding.
